name: workflow-yaml-guard
title: Workflow YAML Guard
description: GitHub Actions review: pull_request_target or workflow_run jobs that check out PR code, untrusted ${{ github.event.* }} in run scripts, actions on movable tags, missing or write-all permissions, echoed secrets and fork-reachable self-hosted runners, with one-tap fixes.

meta.stops: Helps catch workflows that could leak repo secrets to a pull request
meta.summary: Flags GitHub Actions workflow patterns that can expose secrets or the repo to pull requests, following GitHub's secure-use guidance.
meta.server: Also enforce branch protection, required reviews and restricted token permissions in repository settings.
catches: pull_request_target / workflow_run jobs that check out the PR's code (pwn requests)
Untrusted event fields and head_ref interpolated into run scripts
Actions pinned to tags instead of a full commit SHA (pin via your resolveSha)
Secrets echoed, dumped with toJSON or transformed past log masking
Self-hosted runners reachable from fork PRs in public repos
limits: A lightweight, line-aware YAML reader: anchors, complex flow syntax and reusable workflows may be missed
Pattern-based review; it does not prove a workflow is safe
Composite actions and called workflows are not followed
a11y: Visible <label>; aria-invalid and a role=status issue count
Each issue has a button that selects its line, with an aria-label
After a fix, focus moves to the next fix or back to the textarea

rules.note: Confirmed guidance on using an intermediate environment variable for untrusted input and pinning actions to a full-length commit SHA. GitHub Security Lab's pwn-request articles were not re-fetched this round.
